intro: Shared language reduces arguments about tools. Working definitions for this notebook — not a standards body.

terms.def: The durable layer around a model: skills, rules, memory, patterns, and human gates that make agent work reliable and repeatable.
A thin, named procedure loaded on demand when a task matches. How to do a job — not an always-on essay.
A constraint the agent must honour. Prefer requestable (pull when relevant); reserve always-on for Priority 0 (P0) fail-closed constraints only.

The highest-priority, fail-closed constraints that stay always-on in the agent harness. In this notebook’s starter pack there are two: (1) never put secrets in chat — capture into Bitwarden, (2) get explicit human approval before irreversible send/publish/destroy. A “P0 gate” is that human approval step. Not every rule is P0 — most should be requestable.

Prefer moving files to the OS trash or a project trash folder over hard delete (rm). Recovery stays possible until trash is emptied on purpose. A signed pattern — not a third always-on P0 in the starter pack.
A cross-cutting way of working with an explicit lifecycle: propose → human sign-off → encode → apply → review.
Curated durable facts and decisions in a searchable store. Not a raw transcript landfill.
Our durable-memory system: winged rooms, drawers, and a light knowledge graph. Agents search and file on purpose; they do not treat the palace as a chat backup.
Continuous improvement with teeth: observe → propose → human sign-off → encode → apply. No silent policy.
Honest reflection after work or on a cadence: what worked, what failed, keep / amend / retire. Feeds the next Kaizen.
Umbrella name for the lean learning cluster (Kaizen/Hansei, poka-yoke, muda/jidoka, shoshin, kyosei, respect for people). Map to the member practice that matches the pain.
Go see the real work. Start improvements from evidence in the session, not from slogans.
A runtime policy and audit plane for agent tool use. Layer under human Priority 0 (P0) gates — do not replace send/secrets/irreversible consent. Docs: docs.preloop.ai
A multi-model API router across providers, with provider failover and optional model fallbacks. Transport for model calls — not a substitute for skills, rules, or proof class.

A GitHub commit status (context `preloop`) posted by a Preloop Cloud pull-request reviewer after it looks at a PR SHA. CI can optionally wait on that status before burning self-hosted runners. Separate plane from Preloop’s desktop MCP firewall in Cursor.
Human credential vault. Logins and passwords live here — captured via desktop dialog, never pasted into the AI chat.
Machine-secret plane for API tokens and agent-resolvable keys. Isolates captured tokens from the conversation and from the human Password Manager vault.
An explicit approval step before irreversible action (send, publish, destroy, spend). The referent must be visible.
The evidence that counts as done for a task class — tests, logs, screenshots, schema checks — agreed in advance.
A named agent focus with clear owns / never / handoff rules so parallel work does not collide.
Time spent writing skills, signing patterns, and maintaining gates. Real investment — not pure waste, not free speed.
The primary agentic environment where reading the tree, running tools, and leaving diffs is normal.
A WhatsApp personal-assistant channel for monitor/triage and tiered replies, with the same fail-closed outbound rules as the cockpit.
Deliberate reduction of always-on context tax: thin skills, requestable rules, lean MCP sessions, measure and cut catalog bloat.
A desktop multiple-choice dialog for decision forks — preferred over markdown A/B/C walls when a careful human choice is required.
The canonical artefact (usually git markdown for specs). Exports (DOCX/PDF) and Drive mirrors are views — not the SoT.

faq.q: Is a giant system prompt a harness?
faq.a: No. A harness is versioned, selective, and maintained. A giant always-on prompt is usually an unbudgeted tax.
Rules first for fail-closed safety. Then one skill born from a repeated failure. Patterns come once you see the same lesson across domains.

faq.q: Do I need multi-agent lanes on day one?
faq.a: No. Earn them. Lanes help when one chat is thrashing across unrelated owns; they hurt when coordination overhead exceeds the work.

faq.q: How do I know the harness is working?
faq.a: Fewer repeated failures, faster recovery with the same proof class, and less re-explaining decisions. Not “more tokens used”.
Yes — playbooks, templates, and patterns travel well. Keep secrets and credentials out of the published tree.

faq.q: Where does MemPalace fit vs skills?
faq.a: Skills/rules are procedures and constraints. MemPalace holds durable facts the loop needs (decisions, stances, tickets). Both compound; neither replaces the other.

faq.q: What is Kaizen → Hansei → Toyota Way Practices?
faq.a: Kaizen improves and encodes; Hansei reviews honestly; Toyota Way Practices names the lean practice cluster so agents pick the right lens. Sequence: Gemba → Kaizen → Apply → Hansei → repeat.

Priority 0 — the short list of fail-closed, always-on agent rules. The starter pack’s two are: secrets never in chat, and a human gate before irreversible send/publish. Everything else should stay requestable so the always-on tax stays small.
No. Layer it under Priority 0 (P0) gates. Humans still own irreversible outbound and secrets. Preloop adds audit/policy on tool runtime.

To avoid single-upstream lock-in: route across providers, fail over, and optionally fall back across models — while keys stay in a vault and proof class still applies. Same transport can serve Preloop’s PR reviewer.

faq.q: How do Preloop and OpenRouter check PR commits?
faq.a: Preloop Cloud runs a pull-request reviewer on the push; OpenRouter is the model path. Preloop posts a GitHub commit status (`preloop`). Actions can wait on that status before expensive jobs, or leave reviews async. Humans still merge.

faq.q: Is WhatsApp part of the harness?
faq.a: As a channel, yes — triage, tiered replies, and voice as a medium, with the same fail-closed outbound rules as the cockpit.

faq.q: How do you keep tokens under control?
faq.a: Thin skill dispatchers, requestable-by-default rules, enable/unload specialty tools, split parallel lanes, and measure the always-on tax when sessions feel heavy.

faq.q: Where do API keys and passwords go?
faq.a: Not into chat. Desktop capture into Bitwarden — Password Manager for human logins, Bitwarden Secrets Manager for machine/agent secrets — so values never enter the model context or transcript.

faq.q: How often is this notebook updated?
faq.a: During end-of-week (EOW) reviews — not daily. If the week earned a blog note, pack tweak, or pattern change, ship it then. Skip empty weeks; no filler.
